Definition
[Laplace--Beltrami operator on a hypersurface]1. ch16:16.12\group chapter-16 For $g\in C^2(\mathcal U)$ define egin{equation} ag {16.12} \Delta g=\delta _i\delta _i g. \end{equation}

For $\varphi \in C_0^2(\mathcal U)$, (16.10) gives egin{equation} \int _{\mathcal G}\varphi \Delta g\, dA =\int _{\mathcal G}g\Delta \varphi \, dA =-\int _{\mathcal G}\delta g\cdot \delta \varphi \, dA. ag {16.13} \end{equation} For $y\in \mathcal G$, $r=|x-y|$, and a radial function $\psi (r)$, egin{equation} \Delta \psi (r)= rac{n\psi '}r +\left(\psi ''- rac{\psi '}r ight)|\delta r|^2 + rac{n\psi '}rH u \cdot (x-y), ag {16.14} \end{equation} where $|\delta r|^2=1-| u \cdot (x-y)|^2/r^2$. For nonnegative, nonincreasing $\chi \in C^1(\mathbb R)$ supported in $(-\infty ,1)$, set \[ \psi (r)=\int _r^\infty au \chi ( au / ho )\, d au , \] where $0< ho <R$ and $B_R(y)\subset \mathcal U$. Then egin{equation} egin{aligned} \Delta \psi (r) & = ho ^{n+1}D_ ho [ ho ^{-n}\chi (r/ ho )] + rac r ho \chi ’(r/ ho )(1-|\delta r|^2)\ & \qquad -n\chi (r/ ho )H u \cdot (x-y)\ & \le ho ^{n+1}D_ ho [ ho ^{-n}\chi (r/ ho )] -n\chi (r/ ho )H u \cdot (x-y). \end{aligned} ag {16.15} \end{equation} When $H=0$ this reduces to egin{equation} \Delta \psi (r)\le ho ^{n+1}D_ ho [ ho ^{-n}\chi (r/ ho )]. ag {16.16} \end{equation} Suppose $g\ge 0$ is weakly subharmonic on a minimal hypersurface, so egin{equation} \int _\mathcal Gg\Delta \varphi \, dA\ge 0 ag {16.17} \end{equation} for nonnegative $\varphi \in C_0^2(\mathcal U)$. Equations (16.16)--(16.17) make egin{equation} I_\chi ( ho )= rac1{\omega _n ho ^n} \int _\mathcal Sg\chi (r/ ho )\, dA ag {16.18} \end{equation} nondecreasing. Approximation by characteristic cutoffs gives the same property for egin{equation} I( ho )= rac1{\omega _n ho ^n} \int _{\mathcal S\cap B_ ho (y)}g\, dA, ag {16.19} \end{equation} and differentiation of surface measure gives egin{equation} \lim _{ ho o 0}I( ho )=g(y). ag {16.20} \end{equation} Consequently egin{equation} g(y)\le rac1{\omega _nR^n} \int _{\mathcal S\cap B_R(y)}g\, dA. ag {16.21} \end{equation}
